words.def: To stop doing something or leave something behind.
words.note: Say abandon a plan, not abandon from a plan. The verb doesn't need a preposition.

ex.en: They had to *abandon* the car in the snow.
ex.ar: اضطروا إلى ترك السيارة في الثلج.

col.en: We had to *abandon* the plan because it was too expensive.
Don't *abandon* hope. Things can still change.

words.def: The skill or power to do something.

col.en: The job requires the *ability* to learn quickly.
He has a natural *ability* to communicate with people.

words.def: Having the skill, knowledge or opportunity to do something.
words.note: Say I can help you or I'm able to help you, not I am can help you.

col.en: I'll be *able* to help you tomorrow.
I'm not *able* to access my account.

words.def: To say yes to something offered or suggested.

col.en: She decided to *accept* the job offer.
You should *accept* responsibility for your mistakes.

texts.title: Text 1 – A hard decision
texts.en:
Sara had a big plan. She wanted to open a small shop, but it was too expensive, so she had to *abandon|abandon* the idea. At first she felt sad. Then her brother said, "You have the *ability|ability* to learn fast. You will be *able|able* to try again."

Sara thought about it for a week. In the end she decided to *accept|accept* a job in a bookshop. "I will never *abandon|abandon* hope," she said.
texts.ar:
كانت لدى سارة خطة كبيرة. أرادت أن تفتح متجرًا صغيرًا، لكنه كان مكلفًا جدًا، فاضطرت إلى التخلي عن الفكرة.

فكرت سارة في الأمر أسبوعًا، وفي النهاية قررت أن تقبل وظيفة في مكتبة. قالت: «لن أفقد الأمل أبدًا».
